text: {"summary":"The repaired gate correctly broadens the image-evidence-gap path to CSS background PNG/JPEG/WebP subjects while keeping inspectable source indications at unverified, and the new tests cover both directions. I found one reproducible detection gap: the CSS source pattern in assessmentRiskPresentation does not match common url()/relative CSS forms that the test fixture itself uses differently, so some genuine CSS background subjects fall through to unverified.","findings":[{"severity":"P2","file":"lib/assessment-display.ts","line":45,"title":"CSS background image detector misses url(...) forms, contradicting its own test fixture","evidence":"quotesImage regex is /<img\\b|(?:background(?:-image)?\\s*:)[^;}]*\\.(?:png|jpe?g|webp)\\b/iu. The test at tests/assessment-display.test.ts:71 uses excerpt 'background-image: url(\"assets/poster.webp\");' and passes only because the '.webp' substring appears after 'background-image:'. A very common form 'background: url(poster.png) no-repeat;' still contains the extension, so it matches. However 'background-image: var(--hero);' or 'background: url(/img/hero) no-repeat;' with extension-less URLs (extension only on disk) will not match, so a real CSS background subject is classified unverified.","reproduction":"Call assessmentRiskPresentation with coverage.omittedFiles containing a .png, and a risk whose citation excerpt is 'background-image: url(/assets/hero);' (extension-less URL) with content asking to inspect image pixels/subject. quotesImage is false, so kind is 'unverified_source_indication' even though a raster file was excluded and the risk is about CSS background subject.","suggestion":"If extension-less CSS URL forms are in scope, extend the CSS alternative to also match url(...) not followed by a raster extension is not safe; document that only extension-bearing CSS backgrounds are gated, or add a test that extension-less CSS url() stays unverified and note the limitation."},{"severity":"P3","file":"tests/assessment-display.test.ts","line":70,"title":"CSS background test does not exercise the negative case for CSS source issues with raster citation","evidence":"The 'unseen CSS background subject' test reuses the same citation 'background-image: url(\"assets/poster.webp\")' in sourceIssue (tests/assessment-display.test.ts:73) and asserts unverified only because title/explanation/suggestion no longer trip aboutImageSubject/asksForObservation. It does not guard against regex overreach where a CSS source defect that happens to mention 'image' subject words could be misclassified.","reproduction":"Construct risk with citation 'background-image: url(\"assets/poster.webp\")' and explanation that legitimately discusses image with no missing-pixel intent, e.g. 'The image has no alt or aria-label on the decorative background.' aboutImageSubject and quotesImage are true; classify by asksForObservation. If a future edit loosens asksForObservation, it becomes image_evidence_gap incorrectly.","suggestion":"Add an explicit negative test where a CSS background citation with a raster file exists alongside inspectable source phrasing (e.g. missing fallback plus the word 'image') and assert unverified, to lock in the intended boundary."}]}
